aspects.fertilizer:
**General:**
Balanced fertilizer use is essential for better yield and protection against climate change effects.
Determine per-acre fertilizer quantities based on laboratory soil tests.
Apply recommended fertilizer rates for average fertility soils.

**Nutrient requirements for Toria and UAF-11:**
Required nutrients per acre are 23 kg nitrogen, 23 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potash.

**Fertilizer options at sowing:**
Option one is one bag DAP and half bag SOP per acre.
Option two is two and a half bags SSP 18 percent, one-third bag Urea, and half bag SOP per acre.
Option three is three-fourths bag Nitrophos, one and three-fourths bags SSP 18 percent, and half bag SOP per acre.

**Rain-fed barani areas:**
Apply the entire quantity of fertilizer at sowing time.

**Irrigated areas:**
Apply all phosphorus, all potash, and one-third of nitrogen at sowing time.
Divide the remaining nitrogen into two equal splits.
Apply half of the remaining nitrogen with the first irrigation.
Apply the other half of the remaining nitrogen before flowering.

**Additional nutrients and substitutes:**
Apply 4 to 5 kg sulfur per acre with the second irrigation to improve yield and quality.
Use Ammonium Sulphate instead of Urea if it is available.
Boron application is beneficial for increased flowering and pollination.
MOP can be used if SOP is not available, but 2 kg sulfur per acre must be applied with it.

**Private company seed:**
Apply fertilizer according to the rates recommended by the private seed companies.

**Punjab tools and testing:**
Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore developed a free mobile app named Khad Hisab available on Google Play Store.
The app provides balanced fertilizer recommendations for Toria and other crops with or without a soil test report.
Watch the short video in the app introduction box to learn how to use it.
Contact the nearest government soil and water testing laboratory for further information.
aspects.harvesting:
**All Punjab - Toria-A:**
Toria-A is suitable for all Punjab.
Its sowing time is from 15 August to 30 September.
Its harvesting time is from 20 December to 15 January.
Toria-A matures in 90 to 100 days.
Typical yield is 10 to 12 maunds per acre.
Seed oil content is 44 percent.
Insects are required for pollination, and yield can be affected if insect numbers decrease during flowering.
This variety is commonly cultivated for saag.

**Harvesting and Storage:**
Toria must be well dried before storage.
Seed moisture content must be 8 percent and must not exceed 8 percent.
The grain makes a crackling sound when chewed with teeth.
High moisture causes a risk of fungal attack on seeds.
Do not mix seeds of different varieties during storage.
Regularly inspect warehouses to protect stored produce from pest attacks.
Fumigate stores against insect attacks using 30 to 35 tablets of Aluminium Phosphide per 1000 cubic feet.

**Crop Spraying and Safety:**
Use a flat fan nozzle or a flood jet nozzle for weed control in Toria.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect control.
Bury empty poison bottles in the ground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.

**Domestic Oil Refining:**
Extract raw oil using an expeller or kohlu.
Purifying oil at the domestic level makes it relatively cheap, free of impurities, nutritious, and usable as cooking oil.
Put 5 kilograms of raw Toria oil in a pot or pan and heat it to 85 degrees Celsius.
Do not let the oil boil, but ensure the pot becomes too hot to touch.
Add 150 grams of finely ground Fuller's earth or gachni to the hot oil.
Stir thoroughly with a spoon for 5 minutes, then remove it from the stove.
Make a triangular bag from thick market cloth and hang it from a sturdy stand or charpai.
Place a clean vessel underneath the bag.
Pour the lukewarm oil into the triangular cloth bag to filter it.
aspects.irrigation:
Termite Protection:
Flood 1 liter per acre of Fipronil 5 percent SC with water to protect Toria from termite attack.

Water Management:
Take special care of irrigation in the Toria crop during drought.
Sow the crop on ridges to protect it from the effects of heavy rains.
Ridge sowing minimizes crop damage and makes it easy to drain excess water from the field.

General Care and Weather:
Sow the crop at the recommended time for better care of Toria.
Take special care of plant protection.
Stay informed about the weather forecast before sowing the crop or when applying water.
aspects.machinery:
Land Preparation and Drill Sowing:
Prepare the land thoroughly for canola, taramira, toria, and raya crops.
Use a laser land leveler for leveling the land.
Sow the crop in moist soil (tar wattar).
Sow in rows at a distance of 1 to 1.5 feet, maintaining a row-to-row spacing of 1.5 feet.
Maintain a plant population of 60,000 to 70,000 plants per acre.
A small seed drill is available for sowing these crops and gives very good results.
Keep seed depth to no more than 1 to 1.5 inches.

Ridge Sowing:
For ridge planting of toria, broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation.
Run a plow and plank, then create ridges at a distance of 2.5 feet using a tractor.
A planter named ridger-cum-seeder is available in the market from various companies for this planting method.

Spraying Machinery and Safety:
Check the machine with plain water before spraying toria to determine the required water volume.
Use the recommended water quantity to ensure uniform spray application.
Do not stand against the wind direction during spraying.
Do not spray during strong winds.
Avoid using pesticides from the same chemical group repeatedly.
Use a flat fan nozzle or a floodjet nozzle for weed control in toria.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect control.
Bury empty pesticide bottles underground.
Dispose of cardboard packaging boxes.
aspects.other:
Saag harvesting:
Farmers commonly pick saag from the Toria crop.
Picking saag increases the risk of aphid attack.
Picking saag reduces crop yield.
Allocate a separate area for harvesting saag if Toria is grown for seed.
This prevents damage to the remaining seed crop.

Climate change management:
Climate change causes harmful effects on Toria through drought and unexpected heavy rainfall.
Sow the crop at the recommended time to protect it from climate change impacts.
Ensure proper plant protection.
Check the weather forecast before sowing or irrigating.

High rainfall areas:
Sow the crop on ridges in areas with high rainfall.

Training programs:
Training programs for Toria are organized at the district and tehsil level.
Agricultural experts introduce modern cultivation technology to farmers and the Agriculture Department extension staff.
aspects.overview:
**Punjab Production Statistics:**
In 2020-21, Punjab toria area was 413.50 thousand acres (167.34 thousand hectares), total production was 267.26 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 16.16 maunds per acre.
In 2021-22, Punjab toria area was 585.50 thousand acres (236.94 thousand hectares), total production was 403.00 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 17.21 maunds per acre.
In 2022-23, Punjab toria area was 1055.10 thousand acres (426.98 thousand hectares), total production was 665.71 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.77 maunds per acre.
In 2023-24, Punjab toria area was 605.20 thousand acres (244.91 thousand hectares), total production was 314.47 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 12.99 maunds per acre.
According to 2024-25 provisional estimates, Punjab toria area was 820.65 thousand acres (332.10 thousand hectares), total production was 499.94 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.23 maunds per acre.

**Economic Importance:**
Toria is vital for fulfilling edible oil and banaspati ghee requirements.
Domestic edible oil production cannot meet national demand, causing heavy spending of foreign exchange on imports.
Promoting toria cultivation reduces the import bill.
The promotion plan covers oilseed crops including canola, mustard, toria, raya, taramira, linseed, and camelina.

**Variety Toria-A:**
Toria-A matures in 90 to 100 days.
Its seed contains 44 percent oil.
Its typical yield is 10 to 12 maunds per acre.
The variety is commonly cultivated for saag.
Pollination requires insects, so yield is adversely affected if insect populations decline during flowering.

**Soil Requirements:**
Well-drained medium to heavy loam soils are suitable for toria, canola, mustard, and raya.
Highly saline and waterlogged soils are unsuitable for cultivation.

**Rain-fed Areas:**
Toria is cultivated as a Rabi crop using conserved summer monsoon soil moisture.
Techniques should be used to absorb and store summer rainwater in the soil instead of letting it run off.
Properly preserving monsoon rainwater increases Rabi toria yield by 20 to 25 percent.

**Agricultural Extension:**
Toria promotion begins with the publication of a production plan.
Agricultural extension staff writes recommendations and slogans on walls, milestones, and signboards.
The Deputy Director of Agriculture Extension prepares a district strategy, informs the provincial government, and mobilizes staff toward targets.
The Directorate General of Agricultural Information conducts an awareness campaign through print, electronic, and social media from sowing through harvesting.
aspects.pests_diseases:
General Crop Resistance:
Toria has excellent resistance against diseases, insects, and shattering. 

Seed Treatment:
Apply recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kilogram of seed. Do not increase the chemical dose and use appropriate water to avoid harming germination. For stem rot prevention, treat seed at sowing with thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kilogram of seed. Avoid early sowing, rotate crops, destroy weeds, and use treated seed to control collar rot and damping off. Use resistant varieties, crop rotation, and fungicide-treated seed against seedling blight.

Harvesting Practice:
Plucking leaves for saag increases aphid attack risk and reduces yield. Reserve a separate area for saag in seed crops.

Storage:
Inspect warehouses regularly. Fumigate stored toria using 30 to 35 tablets of aluminum phosphide per 1000 cubic feet against insect attacks.

Termites:
Termites attack underground plant parts mostly in dry weather, drying plants so they pull out easily. Apply recommended poison in empty fields during rauni. If attack occurs, flood with irrigation water at 1 liter of fipronil 5 percent SC per acre.

Barani Areas:
Before sowing in rain-fed areas, mix recommended poison with 15 to 20 kilograms of fine soil, broadcast in the field, and plow.

Tokka Grasshopper:
Attack occurs occasionally, with higher risk near sugarcane, maize, and sorghum. Spray per acre with 330 ml lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or 250 ml bifenthrin 10 EC.

Mustard Sawfly:
Larvae attack in October and November. Spray per acre with 80 ml spinetoram 120 SC, 330 ml lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 percent EC, 200 ml emamectin benzoate 1.9 EC, or 30 grams fipronil 80 WG.

Painted Bug:
Nymphs and adults attack in October and November. Spray per acre with 400 ml abamectin plus thiamethoxam 108 SC, 100 grams dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 250 grams acephate 75 SP, or 250 ml bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cabbage Butterfly:
Spray per acre with 80 ml chlorantraniliprole plus thiamethoxam 300 SC, 80 ml spinetoram 120 SC, 50 ml flubendiamide 480 SC, or 250 ml lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC.

Mustard Aphid:
Aphids attack in clusters from mid-January to late March. Complete sowing in the first week of October. Spray per acre with 24 grams thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 grams dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 60 grams flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 ml clothianidin 20 EC.

Biological Control Punjab:
Use green lacewing or Chrysoperla cards against aphids to reduce pesticide use. Agriculture Extension Punjab provides free cards from 11 biocontrol laboratories located in Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Layyah, Vehari, Pakpattan, Sheikhupura, Jhang, Muzaffargarh, Okara, and Toba Tek Singh.

White Rust:
Spray propiconazole or difenoconazole at 1.25 ml per liter of water when white spots appear in cold, humid weather.

Alternaria Blight:
Use healthy seed, rotate crops, and destroy residues. If temperature is 10 to 25 degrees Celsius and raining, spray before symptoms with tebuconazole plus trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or azoxystrobin plus difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

Downy Mildew:
Spray flumorph plus fosetyl-aluminum at 5 grams per liter of water, or mancozeb plus cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter of water. Use healthy seeds and destroy crop residues.

Bacterial Stem Rot:
Under continuous smog, spray per liter of water with 2.5 ml benzothiazolinone, 1 gram streptomycin sulfate, or 6 ml kasugamycin.

Stem Rot:
Spray azoxystrobin plus difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

Blight:
Spray tebuconazole plus trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or metiram plus pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter of water.

Rust:
Spray tebuconazole plus trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or propiconazole at 2 ml per liter of water.

Application Safety:
Spray only when pests or diseases reach economic injury levels. Avoid spraying in strong wind or facing opposite the wind. Spray in the evening to protect pollinators, ladybird beetles, syrphid flies, and Chrysoperla. Use hollow cone nozzles for insects and diseases, and flat fan or flood jet nozzles for weeds. Never hoe immediately after spraying. Wear glasses, gloves, and long rubber boots.
aspects.sowing:
**Punjab Variety and Timing:**
Toria-A is suitable for all of Punjab.
Sowing time is from 15 August to 30 September.
Harvesting time is from 20 December to 15 January.

**General Sowing and Land Preparation:**
Prepare the land thoroughly and level it using a laser land leveler.
Sow in wet moisture conditions (tar wattar).
Row-to-row spacing should be 1 to 1.5 feet.
A small seed drill is available for sowing and gives good results.
Seed depth must not exceed 1 to 1.5 inches.
Maintain a plant population of 60,000 to 70,000 plants per acre.
Check weather forecasts before sowing or applying irrigation.

**Ridge Sowing:**
For ridge sowing, broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation, run a plow and plank, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A ridger-cum-seeder planter is commercially available for this method.
Sowing on ridges minimizes crop damage from heavy rains and makes draining excess water easier.
Take special care of irrigation in drought conditions.

**Sugarcane Intercropping:**
Toria can be intercropped with September-sown sugarcane.
Sow one line of toria between sugarcane lines spaced 2.5 feet apart.
Sow two lines of toria between sugarcane lines spaced 4 feet apart.
Use a seed rate of 1 kg per acre.
This method gives additional oilseed yield and protects the sugarcane crop from frost.

**Rain-fed (Barani) Areas:**
To conserve rainwater moisture, deep plow fallow fields before the monsoon rains.
Strengthen field bunds, plow as needed, level the land, and plow across the slope.
Do not plow after the monsoon season.
Plow twice and plank before sowing so moisture is not lost.
Prepare the land in the evening or before sunrise to prevent moisture loss during preparation.
The field must be level and weed-free at sowing time.

**Thinning:**
Thinning is extremely critical and must be done before the first irrigation.
Thin the crop when plants reach the four-leaf stage.
Remove weak and diseased plants during thinning.
Maintain a distance of 9 to 12 inches between healthy plants.

**Weed Control:**
For drill or wattar sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre before the final plowing.
For ridge sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
aspects.varieties:
**Varieties:**
Recommended varieties include Toria-A, Barani Star, Sarson D.G.L., Barani Sarson, and UAF-11. Farmers should sow disease-resistant varieties.

**Seed Sources:**
Limited seed is available from Punjab Seed Corporation, National Agricultural Research Centre Islamabad, Oilseeds Department at Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad, Oilseeds Research Station Khanpur, Regional Agricultural Research Institute Bahawalpur, and Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal. Certified seed is also available from registered private seed companies. Farmers must always use seed certified by the Federal Seed Certification Department.

**Sowing and Land Preparation:**
Prepare the field well and level it with a laser leveler. Excellent soil moisture is required for proper emergence. Sowing depth must not exceed 1.5 inches. Avoid early sowing of toria.

**Seed Rates:**
Use clean, healthy seed with at least 80 percent germination. The irrigated seed rate is 1.5 to 2 kg per acre. The barani rain-fed seed rate is 1.5 to 2 kg or 2 to 2.5 kg per acre. In Cholistan, the seed rate is 3 to 4 kg per acre.

**Sugarcane Intercropping:**
Short-duration varieties including Toria, UAF-11, AARI Canola, and TM Canola can be intercropped with September-planted sugarcane. Plant 1 oilseed row if sugarcane rows are 2.5 feet apart. Plant 2 oilseed rows if sugarcane rows are 4 feet apart. Use a seed rate of 1 kg per acre. This provides extra yield and protects sugarcane from frost.

**General Seed Treatment:**
Treat seed before planting with recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kg of seed. Strictly avoid overdosing the chemical and use appropriate water volume to prevent germination damage. Do not apply fungicide if proper care cannot be maintained.

**Epidemic Blight:**
Use healthy seed, rotate crops, and destroy plant residues. When temperatures are 10 to 25 degrees Celsius during rainfall, spray before symptoms appear. Spray tebuconazole plus trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or azoxystrobin plus difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

**Downy Mildew:**
Use healthy seed and destroy crop residues. When symptoms appear, spray flumorph plus fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams per liter of water, or mancozeb plus cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter of water.

**Stem Rot:**
Treat seed at sowing with thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kg of seed. If disease appears in the crop, spray azoxystrobin plus difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

**Wilting and Root Rot:**
Symptoms include rotting seed, wilting and drying plants, and split root bark. Control this by treating seed with recommended fungicide, eradicating weeds, rotating crops, and avoiding early planting.

**Plant Blight:**
Sow resistant varieties, practice crop rotation, and treat seed with recommended fungicide. When symptoms appear, spray tebuconazole plus trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or metiram plus pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter of water.
aspects.weeds:
Barani areas:
Deep plow empty fields before monsoon rains to conserve moisture.
Strengthen field bunds.
Plow as needed, level the land, and plow across the slope.
Do not plow after the rainy season.
Before sowing, plow twice and plank to avoid losing moisture.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise to prevent moisture loss.
Fields must be level and weed-free at the time of sowing.

Common weeds:
Weeds commonly found in Toria fields include wild oats, dumbi sitti, lashkni booti, bathu, karand, shahtra, and it-sit.

Non-chemical weed control:
The dab method is very suitable for non-chemical weed control.
In the dab method, plow and apply heavy planking after soaking irrigation or rain when soil has workable moisture, then leave the field for 5 to 7 days.
Emerging weeds will be destroyed during final land preparation.
Perform dry hoeing after crop emergence, preferably before rain, to destroy weeds.
Perform the first hoeing before the first irrigation.
Perform the second hoeing after irrigation when the soil reaches workable moisture.
Thin the crop at the four-leaf stage to maintain recommended plant spacing.

Chemical weed control:
If high weed emergence is expected, apply recommended chemicals immediately after sowing.
In moderate weather when temperatures are 35 degrees Celsius or lower, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing.
For drill and workable moisture sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final plowing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
Apply pre-emergence pendimethalin at 1000 ml per acre.
To control it-sit emerged within two weeks of crop emergence, spray 400 to 500 ml Betazachlor 50 percent SC per acre.
Betazachlor can be sprayed without using a shield.

Application methods and precautions:
Use a flat fan or floodjet nozzle for weed control sprays.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect sprays.
Bury empty chemical bottles in the soil and destroy cardboard boxes.
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after spraying herbicide.
Immediate hoeing breaks the chemical effect, allows weeds to regrow, and raises toxic dust that damages farmer health through breathing.

Crop wilt management:
Wilt causes seed rotting, plant drying, and cracked root bark.
Treat seeds with recommended fungicide before planting.
Avoid early sowing of Toria.
Control weeds and rotate crops to manage wilt.
